question: Near absolute zero, how much pressure does it take to freeze ordinary helium solid?
answer: About 25 times air pressure. Helium atoms are so light, and attract each other so weakly, that their quantum jiggle, a motion that persists even at absolute zero, shakes any crystal apart. At ordinary pressure helium would stay liquid at absolute zero itself: the one element that cold alone cannot freeze.
move: Rules learned from ordinary cases can fail at the extremes.
trap: Assuming cold alone freezes everything, as it does every familiar liquid.
source: Wilks & Betts, Introduction to Liquid Helium, 1987
reference: Wilks & Betts, An Introduction to Liquid Helium, 2nd edition, Clarendon Press, Oxford, 1987
